title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation

release_status.value: No official DASH implementation, weight or dataset release verified from the paper and targeted searches.

evidence_boundaries: 20 Hz denotes tested action updates, not VLM context refresh or joint servo rate.
RoboTwin uses ALOHA; real humanoid experiments are quasi-static tabletop manipulation.
0.8B is Qwen3.5 and 2B/4B/8B are Qwen3-VL. Success is highest at 4B in this protocol.
Aligned training on the asynchronous runtime yields equal or lower success than sync.
The real-world comparison changes execution and aggregation jointly; no isolated hardware aggregator ablation.
RoboTwin plans 250 episodes per configuration and computes success over valid initializations.
The freshness and adaptability of the independent vision encoder are not separately isolated.
